description: CTO CROSS-MISSION CONTEXT ISOLATION §B: the validation-engine (authoritative verdict) does NOT verify that patch-execution.json belongs to the same mission as mission-plan.json. REPRODUCED false-success: plan.mission=MISSION_B + patch-execution.mission=MISSION_A ⇒ status=SUCCESS validated=true (MISSION_B 'covered' by MISSION_A's execution). self-diagnostic already guards this (detectDivergences §0 mission-context-stale); the validation-engine must have parity. Add a fail-closed mission-ownership guard: plan.mission && execution.mission both known and DIFFERENT ⇒ BLOCKED (never SUCCESS/PARTIAL), with an explicit unmet reason. Backward compatible: either identity unknown (legacy unstamped) ⇒ unchanged. Both ports. No new primitive; mirrors the existing self-diagnostic guard.

authorization.authorization_source: CTO CROSS-MISSION CONTEXT ISOLATION & INCIDENT CLOSURE V4 §B (fix the demonstrated common-cause defect with the smallest safe write-set).

work_item_contract.objective: validation-engine refuses to produce a SUCCESS/PARTIAL verdict when mission-plan.json and patch-execution.json belong to DIFFERENT missions; it BLOCKS with an explicit cross-mission reason. Parity with self-diagnostic detectDivergences §0.
work_item_contract.claim_reproduction_rootcause: REPRODUCED (temp cwd): plan.mission=MISSION_B, patch-execution.mission=MISSION_A, objectives/planned/executed all =1 ⇒ coverage true ⇒ status=SUCCESS validated=true for MISSION_B using MISSION_A's execution. ROOT CAUSE: the verdict's coverage/evidence gates never check execution.mission === plan.mission (no artifact-ownership guard), while self-diagnostic DOES. PLAN: add a fail-closed cross-mission guard to the verdict.
work_item_contract.scope: validation-engine both ports: compute crossMission (plan.mission && execution.mission && differ) ⇒ force validated=false, status BLOCKED, add unmet reason, exclude from partialEligible, add crossMissionOk to checks. One spawn-based test (historical .js + compiled dist .js). No other gate changed; same-mission + legacy-unstamped behaviour identical.
invariants: FAIL-CLOSED: cross-mission ⇒ BLOCKED, never SUCCESS/PARTIAL. No path turns a cross-mission mismatch green.
BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: when plan.mission or execution.mission is absent (legacy/unstamped), behaviour is UNCHANGED.
Mirrors self-diagnostic §0 (one shared policy; no new primitive).
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce-before: cross-mission ⇒ SUCCESS (defect). After-fix: cross-mission ⇒ BLOCKED validated=false + unmet names plan/execution missions. Same-mission SUCCESS unchanged. Legacy execution without mission ⇒ unchanged. Dual-port .js≡dist verdict parity on the cross-mission case. Non-regression: validation-engine-recorded-noop / gamma / probe-freshness / orchestrator + the validation-engine-equivalence bench ALL PASS. tsc 0. Diff limited to write-set; committed; dist rebuilt.
stop_conditions: A same-mission or legacy-unstamped verdict would change; a path outside the write-set is needed.
work_item_contract.rollback: git checkout -- runtime/core/validation-engine.{ts,js} ODG_PROJECT_STATE.md; rm -f runtime/core/validation-engine-cross-mission.test.ts runtime/missions/VE_CROSS_MISSION_OWNERSHIP_GUARD.json; npm run build:runtime.

objectives.goal: validation-engine fail-closed guards cross-mission artifact mismatch (parity with self-diagnostic); backward compatible; both ports; proven by reproduce-before/after + parity + non-regression.
done_when: All acceptance_criteria met; committed in write-set; dist rebuilt.

definition_of_done: validation-engine refuses a verdict over cross-mission artifacts (BLOCKED), parity with self-diagnostic, backward compatible, both ports; proven reproduce-before/after + parity + non-regression; committed (no force). A fail-closed isolation fix, NOT a status change.
